clue.text: Members of family regularly seen in pieces

indicators.note: in tells us the regular letters go inside the word for pieces

parts.note: pieces are parts

indicators.note: regularly means take every other letter of the word seen

explanation.surface: Relatives keep turning up in fragments, as if the family were scattered.
explanation.definitionFit: Mothers and fathers are the members of a family who raised the children.

clue.text: Sign of fish tank needing base to be changed?

indicators.note: base is the bottom letter of a down entry, here the final letter of the tank word, swapped for another letter

parts.note: a fish tank is an aquarium

explanation.surface: A fish tank seems to want its base replaced, and a zodiac sign is somehow involved.
explanation.walkthrough: The final M of AQUARIUM, its base in a down light, becomes S; the question mark admits the new letter is not clued.
explanation.definitionFit: The Water Carrier is the eleventh sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: Requests variable rent and food

indicators.note: variable means the letters of rent can be arranged differently

parts.note: eats is slang for food

explanation.surface: A tenant asks about a fluctuating rent and meals being included.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to beg or plead, so the verb matches asks earnestly.

clue.text: Goes and covers roof and gates

parts.note: goes, as in 'it's your go', are turns
tiles are what cover a roof

explanation.surface: Someone walks off and covers a roof and some gates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes' is a plural noun, not a verb: turns in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Turnstiles are revolving barriers at entrances, a kind of gate admitting one person at a time.

clue.text: Breeze along full of enthusiasm

indicators.note: full of says the words Breeze along contain the answer inside them

explanation.surface: Someone breezes along, bursting with eagerness.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeal is fervour or eager devotion to a cause.

clue.text: Token working in support of military takeover

indicators.note: in a down entry a supporting piece sits beneath the thing it holds up

parts.note: a coup is a seizure of power by the army
on means working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: A token gesture made in favour of a military takeover.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupon is a voucher or ticket exchanged for goods, a kind of token.

clue.text: 'A', for instance may be six-time African despot

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda

explanation.surface: A grade A pupil, perhaps, might be a six-times African dictator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' looks like a letter or grade; it is the retinol nutrient.
explanation.definitionFit: Retinol, labelled A, is one of the essential nutrients in the lettered series.

clue.text: Journalist on leave finally in New York cab

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the first piece above the next

parts.note: a hack is a journalist, especially a jobbing one

indicators.note: in places the final letter inside the New York abbreviation
finally means take the last letter of leave

explanation.surface: A reporter on holiday takes a taxi in Manhattan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes E from 'leave', put inside NY to make NEY.
explanation.definitionFit: A hackney carriage is the formal British term for a licensed taxi.

clue.text: Poor menials must eat old wheat concoction

indicators.note: must eat says the anagram swallows the abbreviation for old
poor signals the letters of menials are in bad shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: Badly treated servants are made to eat an old wheat-based dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges MENIALS around O to SEM-O-LINA.
explanation.definitionFit: Semolina is coarse durum wheat meal, often cooked into a milky pudding.

clue.text: Gathers Queen is beset by obligations

indicators.note: the queen is surrounded on both sides by the word for obligations

parts.note: musts are things that must be done
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: The monarch rallies her people despite being besieged by duties.
explanation.definitionFit: To muster is to assemble or collect troops or people.

clue.text: Food found by sailor after panic?

indicators.note: the sailor comes after the panic word in the answer

parts.note: a flap is a state of agitation
Jack, as in Jack Tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor finds something to eat after a moment of alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A flapjack is an oat bar in Britain, or a pancake in America; either is a foodstuff.

clue.text: Female censors upset about international art of public debate

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters surround the abbreviation for international
upset means the letters of censors are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman finds the censors upset over something international.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns CENSORS into ORENSCS, wrapped 'about' I to give ORENSICS.
explanation.definitionFit: Forensics, from the Latin forum, is formal argumentation or debating.

clue.text: Welcomes politicians with time for North

indicators.note: time for North means the letter T takes the place of N

parts.note: Greens are members of an environmentalist party

explanation.surface: Politicians are welcomed, with time set aside for northern matters.
explanation.definitionFit: To greet someone is to receive or hail them on arrival.

clue.text: Oily product in nut tree scattered across Portugal

indicators.note: the scattered letters lie across, that is on both sides of, the letter for Portugal
scattered means the letters of in nut tree are rearranged

parts.note: P is the international vehicle code for Portugal

explanation.surface: An oil is found in a nut tree dotted around Portugal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is part of the anagram, not a container word: IN NUT TREE are rearranged around P.
explanation.definitionFit: Turpentine is a volatile oil distilled from pine resin.

clue.text: Abrasive remedy developed with no end of blood daily

indicators.note: developed means the letters of remedy are worked into a new form, here without the letter named
end of takes the last letter of blood

parts.note: a daily is a newspaper

explanation.surface: A cure is developed that has nothing to do with blood, for daily use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes D, the 'end of' blood, from REMEDY; 'developed' rearranges the rest to EMERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Emery paper is coated with powdered corundum and used for smoothing and polishing.

clue.text: Look for regular meeting-place, missing area

indicators.note: missing means the abbreviation for area is left out

parts.note: a haunt is a place frequently visited

explanation.surface: Someone searches for their usual meeting spot, but a district is gone.
explanation.definitionFit: To hunt is to search for something.

clue.text: Separates chips

definitions.meaning: breaks apart into thin fragments, a verb
small sharp slivers of wood or glass, a noun

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means shatters into pieces; as a plural noun, sharp fragments.

clue.text: Such a ship may be ageing so badly

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of ageing so are put in disorder

explanation.surface: An old vessel might be deteriorating so poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as an ageing ship; 'may be' links the definition to the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A seagoing vessel is one fit for ocean voyages rather than coastal or river waters.

clue.text: Tweet may get time in prison and summons

parts.note: bird is British slang for a prison sentence, from rhyming slang bird-lime for time
a call is a summons

explanation.surface: A social media post could land someone in jail and earn a court summons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tweet' suggests a post online; it is the chirp. BIRD is British slang for jail time.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweet is the chirping sound a small songbird makes.

clue.text: Unfavourable notice on output of poet

indicators.note: on in a down clue places the notice above the second piece

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
verse is what a poet produces

explanation.surface: A poor review of a poet's work.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse means hostile or harmful, as in adverse conditions.

clue.text: A source of bacteria in European circus performer

indicators.note: in puts the first letter of bacteria inside the European

parts.note: a Croat is a person from Croatia

indicators.note: source of means take the first letter of bacteria

explanation.surface: A germ source found inside a European performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European' is a specific nationality, CROAT, with B inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrobat performs feats of balance and agility, typically in a circus.

clue.text: Bond is back, welcoming 'Vote leave'

indicators.note: welcoming means the reversed word takes in the voting mark
is back means the word for bond is written in reverse

parts.note: a tie is a bond
X is the mark made on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: James Bond returns to back the Vote Leave Brexit campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: Bond is not 007 but TIE, reversed to EIT; 'Vote leave' looks like the slogan but splits into X and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit is a departure, the act of going out.

clue.text: Give unrestricted access to study group during worship

indicators.note: during means the study group comes inside the word for worship

parts.note: to deify is to worship as a god
a class is a group of students

explanation.surface: A secret is released to a study group in the middle of a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Declassifying a document removes its secrecy so anyone may see it.

clue.text: Value diamonds found in a swamp

indicators.note: found in means the diamonds letter lies inside the other pieces

parts.note: a mire is a bog or swamp
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games

explanation.surface: Precious stones turn up in a bog, and are prized.
explanation.definitionFit: To admire something is to esteem or value it highly.

clue.text: Temple — a party space rejected!

indicators.note: rejected means the pieces are thrown back, read in reverse

parts.note: a do is a party
a gap is a space

explanation.surface: A temple turned down as a venue for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered tower used as a Buddhist or Hindu temple in Asia.

clue.text: Ultimately lose weight, getting room for eating dessert

indicators.note: ultimately means take the last letter of lose

parts.note: a ton is a unit of weight
a mess is a dining room in the armed forces

explanation.surface: Finally shed some pounds, then get a dining hall to eat pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton mess is a British pudding of strawberries, cream and broken meringue.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton mess is a classic summer pudding, named after the school.

clue.text: Evil king's ruin

parts.note: sin is evil or wrongdoing
K is the abbreviation for king in chess

explanation.surface: A wicked monarch brings about his own downfall.
explanation.definitionFit: To sink a plan or a person is to wreck or destroy them.

clue.text: Go for one accountant with line of sight

parts.note: to opt for is to choose, to go for
I is the Roman numeral one
CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: Choose one accountant who has a clear view of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line of sight' looks like a single phrase; 'line' gives L and 'of sight' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Optical means relating to vision or the eyes.

clue.text: Taking the lead from Republican in looking

indicators.note: in puts the Republican letter inside the word for looking

parts.note: staring is looking fixedly

explanation.surface: Someone takes charge away from a Republican while gazing on.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor starring in a film plays the leading role.

clue.text: Easily destroyed dossier penetrated by tabloid

indicators.note: penetrated by means the dossier word is pierced by the tabloid word

parts.note: a file is a dossier
a rag is a disparaging word for a downmarket newspaper

explanation.surface: A sensitive dossier is leaked by a tabloid and so easily ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: Fragile describes something delicate or readily broken.
